subject: ventures/fractional-executive-rate-calculator
professional: a working US fractional CFO who prices their own engagements (and checks clients' self-employment tax), the first things checked being the payroll-tax treatment for a $200k+ earner, the utilisation assumption behind the day rate, and whether the retainer and client-mix figures reconcile

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with scratchpad frac/se.mjs. Pass (hand arithmetic, standard billable-days method): page example (salary 200,000 + bonus 40,000, benefits 30,000, costs 10,000, 7.65%, 260 days, 30 off, 20% non-billable, 80% sold) gives 280,000/0.9235 = 303,194.37, (260-30)*0.8*0.8 = 147.2 sold days, 2,059.74/day, 257.47/h, 2.68x of 200,000/260; the tool and the Chromium page show $303,194, 147, $2,060, $257, 2.7x. Client mix 4+3+5 days at 10% discount: 12*2,059.74*0.9 = 22,245.19/month, 266,942.30/yr, *0.9235 - 40,000 = 206,521.22 left, 33,478.80 short; page shows $266,942, $206,521, $33,479. FTE daily pay 200,000/260 = 769.23 matches the 2,080-hour (260 x 8) convention. Fail: payroll tax against IRS 'Self-employment tax' page and Topic 751 (15.3% on 92.35% of net earnings, Social Security part only on the first $184,500 in 2026, 0.9% additional Medicare above $200,000), net of the employee FICA the salary already bore: the example's extra tax is 15,830, not the tool's 23,194 (46% over), so revenue 295,829.62 vs 303,194.37 (+2.5%) and day rate 2,009.71 vs 2,059.74; a 300,000 CFO is +3.4% (2,526.59 vs 2,611.46); below the base (100,000) the gap is 0.7%. Fail: a blank or 0 'share you expect to sell' silently becomes 100% (calc.mjs:48): page shows $1,648/day over 184 sold days instead of an error. Arithmetic right, the one tax rule wrong for the target earner and a silent fallback: 2.
evidence.completeness: Walked in Chromium via Playwright at 375 px (scratchpad frac/walk.cjs, files served by route interception): Load an example computes (day rate, 5 retainer rows 2-10 days, client table, mix table, 5 findings); Calculate after editing working days to 250 recomputes ($2,153, 141 days); bad client line reported as 'Some lines were not read'; Clear then Calculate shows 'Enter the full-time pay'; opt-out sets the stored flag, removes counters and disables the button; usage counter records rate_calculated and example_loaded in localStorage; LICENSE 200; no console errors, no external requests. Every README feature (rateFor, retainerFor, parseClients/analyse, findings) works end to end; no stubs or TODOs: 3.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the subject dir: tests 25, pass 25, fail 0; the README's 'node --test' also passes 25/25. Seven mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: dropping costs from revenue needed caught; discount cap 90 -> 5 caught; capacity check > 1 -> > 1.2 caught; FTE day pay divisor workingDays -> 260 SURVIVED; low-multiple threshold 1.5 -> 3 SURVIVED; concentration threshold 0.5 -> 0.8 SURVIVED; sold fallback || 100 -> || 80 SURVIVED. The headline arithmetic is pinned by a hand-checked test, but 4 of 7 seeded bugs in finding thresholds and input fallbacks pass: 2.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (139 lines), index.html (233 lines incl. script), usage.mjs, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.test.mjs. Pure engine, client names escaped (an client name rendered as text in the walk), storage access guarded, no network. Defects: silent fallbacks for blank/zero inputs (soldPct -> 100, workingDays -> 260, hoursPerDay -> 8, calc.mjs:43,48,51) and silent clamps (payroll tax 50%, non-billable 90%, discount 90%) with no finding; 'takeHome' names gross pre-tax pay (calc.mjs:38); retainerFor returns effectiveDayRate 0 rather than null for 0 days (calc.mjs:69); the client-mix table overflows a 375 px viewport by 2 px (scrollWidth 377, index.html:110). Small and readable: 3.
evidence.claims: Backed: day/hourly/retainer/client-mix outputs (calc.mjs, walk); 'nothing uploaded' (page.test asserts no fetch/XHR/beacon, walk saw no external request); usage events named in the footer equal those recorded; DNT/GPC honoured (usage.mjs); no-warranty and not-advice text in footer and FAQ; 'What this does not cover' lists income tax, equity, collection, market rates; FAQ JSON-LD matches visible copy (page.test); served llms.txt points at marisstella.app (curl of the live llms.txt, served-copy.mjs: no placeholder origin). Wrong or unbacked: index.html:86 'roughly 7.65 percent of revenue extra in the US' is wrong for anyone above the 2026 $184,500 Social Security base (IRS), i.e. most of the stated audience; the same note says time off comes off '260 working days' though the field is editable; the '1.5x employee daily pay' rule (FAQ, JSON-LD, finding) cites nothing; 'take-home' is used for gross pay (defined once in the limits list). 2.
evidence.fitness: Walked as a $200k CFO going fractional: in under a minute the page gives a day rate, hourly rate, retainer prices for 2-10 days a month and whether a three-client book covers the target, with the shortfall and concentration flagged. That is the job ('what do I quote'). First-hour gaps: no profit or risk margin above replacement cost, retainers only as days per month (no hours-per-month or days-per-week framing), no saved or downloadable result, payroll tax overstated by ~2.5-3.4% on revenue for this earner (conservative direction). Usable with stated limits: 3.
evidence.domain: Compared with the standard billable-utilisation (cost-plus) pricing method (target revenue / billable days, with time off and non-billable time removed first) and IRS SE-tax rules (IRS 'Self-employment tax (Social Security and Medicare taxes)' and Topic 751, fetched 2026-11-26). Matches: the utilisation method (147.2 of 260 days, 56.6% billable, within the usual solo-consultant range), treating replaced benefits as a cost, the employer-half framing of the tax change. Departs: payroll tax is a flat share of gross revenue including business costs, rather than 15.3% x 92.35% of net earnings with the Social Security part stopping at the wage base and the employee half netted; no margin; the 1.5x heuristic is uncited. A fractional CFO would accept the rate method and correct the tax line: 2.

defects.what: Payroll tax is a flat 7.65% of gross revenue (business costs included), with no Social Security wage base: for the page's own $240k example the extra tax is 23,194 vs 15,830 under IRS SE-tax rules (15.3% on 92.35% of net earnings, 12.4% part capped at $184,500 in 2026, less the employee FICA already borne), so revenue needed and the day rate are 2.5% high ($2,060 vs $2,010) and 3.4% high for a $300k CFO; only below the base is it within 0.7%

A blank or 0 'share of billable days you expect to sell' silently becomes 100% (nn(...) || 100), so clearing the field to retype it prices against 184 instead of 147 days: $1,648 a day instead of $2,060, with no finding

The payroll-tax note states 'roughly 7.65 percent of revenue extra in the US' (wrong above the $184,500 2026 wage base, where most of the audience sits) and that time off comes off '260 working days' though working days is an editable field
The '1.5x employee daily pay' rule in the FAQ, FAQ JSON-LD and the low-multiple finding cites no source; at default utilisation with zero benefits and costs the model itself already gives 1.91x

Finding thresholds and input fallbacks are untested: FTE day-pay divisor workingDays -> 260, multiple threshold 1.5 -> 3, concentration 0.5 -> 0.8 and sold fallback 100 -> 80 all leave the 25 tests green
The client-mix table overflows a 375 px viewport by 2 px after the example loads (documentElement.scrollWidth 377), giving a small horizontal scroll on phones

The rate is break-even replacement cost with no profit or risk margin input, and retainers are priced only as whole days a month (no hours-per-month or days-per-week framing common in fractional engagements)

verdict: A small, private, well-behaved fractional-executive pricing page whose arithmetic recomputes exactly (example: 280,000/0.9235 = $303,194 over 147.2 sold days = $2,060 a day; the 4+3+5-day mix at 10% off leaves $206,521, $33,479 short) and whose page works end to end at 375 px with 25 passing tests. It does not meet the bar: correctness, verification, claims and domain are 2. The one tax rule it encodes, a flat 7.65% of revenue, ignores the 2026 $184,500 Social Security wage base its $200k+ audience is above, overstating the extra tax by 46% and the day rate by 2.5-3.4%; a blank sold-share field silently prices at 100% sold (20% low); and 4 of 7 seeded mutants in thresholds and fallbacks survive. Finished (completeness 3); a fractional CFO would use the method after correcting the tax line.
